title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Say how you feel, give your opinion, agree and disagree, and link ideas with 'because', 'but' and 'so'.
intro: Many Gujarati emotions are things that 'come to' or 'strike' you, so they use the dative: **મને ગુસ્સો આવે છે** 'I get angry' (lit. 'anger comes to me'), **મને ડર લાગે છે** 'I'm scared'. Opinions use the same pattern: **મને લાગે છે કે…** 'I think that…' (lit. 'it seems to me that…').

grammar.title: Feelings that 'come to' you
grammar.body:
Most emotions are expressed with the dative person + emotion noun + a verb meaning 'come', 'strike' or 'happen':

**આવવું** 'come': મને ગુસ્સો આવે છે (anger), કંટાળો આવે છે (boredom), મજા આવે છે (fun), શરમ આવે છે (embarrassment)
**લાગવું** 'strike, be felt': મને ડર લાગે છે (fear), નવાઈ લાગે છે (surprise), ખરાબ લાગે છે (feel bad)
**થવું** 'happen': મને આનંદ થયો (joy), દુઃખ થયું (sorrow)

Adjectives like **ખુશ** and **દુઃખી** use the ordinary verb 'to be': **હું ખુશ છું**. And 'to be tired' is a verb: **હું થાકી ગયો છું** (lit. 'I have got tired').

examples.en: Did you feel bad? / Were you offended?
I was sad to hear this.

grammar.title: 'I think that…': મને લાગે છે કે
grammar.body:
The usual way to give an opinion is **મને લાગે છે કે …** 'it seems to me that…'. The conjunction **કે** 'that' introduces the clause, which keeps normal word order. More formal: **હું માનું છું કે …** 'I believe that…'.

To disagree gently: **મને એવું નથી લાગતું** 'I don't think so'. To ask someone: **તમને શું લાગે છે?** 'What do you think?'

examples.native: મને લાગે છે કે વરસાદ આવશે.
examples.roman: mane lāge chhe ke varsād āvshe.

examples.native: હું માનું છું કે ગુજરાતી સહેલી છે.
examples.roman: huṃ mānuṃ chhuṃ ke gujarātī sahelī chhe.

examples.native: મને નથી લાગતું કે એ આવશે.
examples.roman: mane nathī lāgtuṃ ke e āvshe.

grammar.title: Linking ideas: કારણ કે, પણ, એટલે
grammar.body:
**કારણ કે** (or **કેમ કે**) 'because' introduces a reason after the main clause.
**પણ** 'but' joins contrasting clauses (remember, after a single word it means 'also').
**એટલે** 'so, that's why' introduces a result. **એટલે જ** = 'that's exactly why'.
**તો** 'then, so' is used to draw a conclusion or in 'if… then' sentences (Unit 19).

examples.native: હું આજે નહીં આવું, કારણ કે મારી તબિયત સારી નથી.

examples.en: The film was long, but it was fun.

examples.roman: bahu garmī hatī, eṭle ame ghare rahyāṃ.
examples.en: It was very hot, so we stayed home.

dialogue.title: After the film
dialogue.setting: Krupa and her cousin Aman leave a cinema after watching a new Gujarati film.

lines.speaker: Aman
lines.en: How did you find the film?

lines.speaker: Krupa
lines.native: મને તો બહુ મજા આવી! ગીતો એકદમ સરસ હતાં.
lines.roman: mane to bahu majā āvī! gīto ekdam saras hatāṃ.
lines.en: I really enjoyed it! The songs were great.

lines.speaker: Aman
lines.native: હા, ગીતો સારાં હતાં, પણ વાર્તા થોડી ધીમી હતી.
lines.roman: hā, gīto sārāṃ hatāṃ, paṇ vārtā thoḍī dhīmī hatī.
lines.en: Yes, the songs were good, but the story was a bit slow.

lines.speaker: Krupa
lines.native: મને એવું નથી લાગતું. છેલ્લે તો હું રડી પડી!
lines.roman: mane evuṃ nathī lāgtuṃ. chhelle to huṃ raḍī paḍī!
lines.en: I don't think so. At the end I actually cried!

lines.speaker: Aman
lines.native: સાચે? મને તો વચ્ચે કંટાળો આવ્યો.
lines.roman: sāche? mane to vachche kaṇṭāḷo āvyo.
lines.en: Really? I got bored in the middle.

lines.speaker: Krupa
lines.native: કારણ કે તું ફોન જોતો હતો!
lines.roman: kāraṇ ke tuṃ fon joto hato!
lines.en: Because you were looking at your phone!

lines.speaker: Aman
lines.native: હા હા, તારી વાત સાચી છે. ખોટું ના લગાડતી.
lines.roman: hā hā, tārī vāt sāchī chhe. khoṭuṃ nā lagāḍtī.
lines.en: Ha ha, you're right. Don't be offended.

lines.speaker: Krupa
lines.native: ના રે! ચાલ, હવે આઇસક્રીમ ખાઈએ.
lines.roman: nā re! chāl, have āiskrīm khāīe.
lines.en: Not at all! Come on, let's have ice cream now.

culture: Gujarati conversation is warm and expressive, but direct disagreement with elders is avoided; softeners like **કદાચ** 'perhaps', **મને લાગે છે** 'I think', and the tag **ને** make opinions sound gentler. Gujarati cinema (Dhollywood) has had a big revival since the 2010s, and Gujarati folk and garba songs are a shared emotional language.
